My land is about 10 mu, same as it's always been. My father grew wheat and maize here, and so do I. That's what this land is for. The soil is flat, the well is shared with the neighbors, and the grain station in town buys both crops at the government support price. I'm not going to try something new and risky — I have a family to feed and loans to repay.

Winter wheat goes in around October after the maize comes off. I'll do rotary tillage to break up the stalks and even out the field before sowing. I use the improved variety everybody around here uses — it handles the dry winters and gives decent yield. Three irrigations: one before freeze-up, one at jointing, one at grain fill. I put down base fertilizer at sowing and top-dress urea after green-up. Two pesticide passes — one herbicide early on, one fungicide and aphid spray in May when things get warm.

Summer maize goes straight in after wheat harvest in June, no-till, because the ground is already worked and I don't want to lose moisture or time. I use hybrid seed, the same kind the seed shop has been selling for years. It yields well. One irrigation if August gets dry at tasseling. Topdress nitrogen at big bell stage. Herbicide right after emergence, one more spray for corn borer.
